title: Shift-Robust Molecular Relational Learning with Causal Substructure

problem.claim: Molecular relational learning aims to predict interaction behavior between molecular pairs.

gap.claim: Existing molecular relational learning needs robustness to distributional shift and must address shortcut substructures spuriously correlated with chemical reactions.

contributions.claim: CMRL detects the core substructure causally related to chemical reactions to improve robustness to distributional shift.
The work constructs a structural causal model based on domain knowledge to represent relationships among variables.
The work introduces a conditional intervention framework whose intervention is conditioned on the paired molecule.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the conditional intervention framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CMRL learns from causal substructure and alleviates confounding from shortcut substructures.
The authors report superiority over state-of-the-art baseline models on various tasks using real-world and synthetic datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Molecular relational learning predicts interaction behavior between molecular pairs and has broad applications.
CMRL is proposed to improve robustness to distributional shift by detecting causally related molecular substructure.
A domain-knowledge-based structural causal model is constructed to reveal variable relationships.
A novel intervention framework conditions intervention on the paired molecule.
The model is reported to learn causal substructure, reduce shortcut confounding, and outperform state-of-the-art baselines across real-world and synthetic datasets.

source_observation.claim: Conditioning intervention on the paired molecule is used to learn causal substructure under distributional shift.

interpretation.claim: Interventions that preserve relevant relational context may help distinguish causal structure from spurious correlations.

application.claim: For paired-entity prediction tasks, consider interventions conditioned on the paired entities when modeling distribution shifts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the assumed causal relationship or conditional intervention will fail.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, tasks, metrics, baseline identities, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, or reproducibility information.
